title: Station job result
description: The body of POST /api/station/jobs/<id> (StationLink._run_job, sizeup/cloud/station.py): the outcome of one job of station-jobs, read by the hub's caller that waits for it (Hub.call, sizeup/cloud/hub.py). <id> is the job's 16 hex characters. Plain JSON, not gzipped, at most 16 MiB. The hub keeps the whole object and reads `ok`, `error`, `result`, `label` and `audio`. Sent once the job is done, tried 3 times in all (a 5xx or no answer: again after 1 s, then 2 s; a 4xx: given up), then dropped (J2). What `result` is depends on the job, which the body does not name: `$defs` has one schema per function of `call` (result.<fn>) and one for sources_reset; a `tts` job answers with `label` and `audio` instead.

ok.description: true: the job ran. false: it did not, or raised; the hub's caller gets `error` as its failure (a falsy value of any type counts as false).

error.description: With ok false: why, for people. An exception is `<Type>: <message>`, cut to 300 characters. Two texts are part of the contract today because the hub looks for the words `not allowed` (D2): `not allowed from the hub: '<fn>'` and `this station doesn't know job '<type>'`.

result.description: With ok true, for `call` and `sources_reset`: what the function returned, any JSON value (null for most switches that worked).

label.description: With ok true, for `tts`: which voice said it, for people (`Voice: ...`).

audio.description: With ok true, for `tts`: the rendered dispatch, standard base64 of a WAV file as the station's voice wrote it (so it starts with `UklGR`, RIFF). The hub decodes it strictly (validate=True) and takes it only if the bytes start with RIFF; nothing else of the WAV is checked. Anything else: the dispatch goes out as text only.

result.set_mode.description: null when the dongle was switched, else why not.

result.set_talkgroup.description: null when set, else why not.

result.set_talkgroup_group.description: null when set, else why not.

result.emergency_all_clear.description: true when an emergency window was open on the station.

queued.description: The clips now waiting for whisper (or already there).

additionalProperties.description: Why: `no recording on the station`, `longer than <n> s`.

refused.description: Per clip id, why it can never be read here; the hub gives those up.

hold.description: Why none was taken now (a station update is waiting); "" when they were.

result.set_adsb_receiver.description: null when set, else why not.

result.set_antenna_groups.description: null when saved, else why not; `confirm: <question>` asks the person first.

result.sources_poll_now.description: How many adapters were woken; 0 on a station with none.

result.reception_post.description: null when done, else why not.

result.reception_sample_b64.description: Standard base64 of a WAV file (so it starts with `UklGR`, RIFF); "" for no such sample.

rev.description: The revision it keeps: the one sent.

result.quarantine_dismiss.description: How many of the station's stuck and late quarantined events of that type were dropped; 0 when none (or no hub link). The hub logs it, audits it with who asked and answers the admin {ok: true, dismissed: n}.

result.stt_withdraw.title: What the station did with each id
result.stt_withdraw.description: App.stt_withdraw's answer (#927): each id it was sent in one of three lists.

withdrawn.description: Taken out of whisper's queue: nothing goes up for them.

running.description: On whisper already: it runs on, and its text stays on the station.

gone.description: Not waiting here: its text went up already, it was never sent at its close, or the station doesn't know it. The hub decides between the texts.

result.sources_reset.description: What was asked of each source, for people: `<source>: reset asked (runs before its next poll)`; the hub keeps 300 characters.
